1.title: Know courier work
1.intro: Couriers move parcels and documents from one place to another on time and safely. Learn the main types and words first.
pts: Name types of courier jobs: same-day, next-day, scheduled routes, medical or legal documents.
Describe the steps: pick-up, scan or sign, carry, deliver, proof.
Explain what proof of delivery is and why it matters.
List words: waybill, manifest, route, dispatch, signature on delivery.
Compare same-day and scheduled routes by price, stress and planning.
Identify what a waybill must show: sender, receiver, contents and time.
Check who is responsible if a parcel is lost by reading the agreement.
1.ex: A law office needs a document at a court by 3 pm. The courier collects at 1 pm, which leaves a 2 hour buffer, gets a signature at the court and sends the proof to the office.
1.act: Follow a delivery you receive. Note every step from order to door.
1.std: Task: name the steps of a delivery. Condition: from a real parcel. Standard: five steps and the proof clearly listed.

2.title: Plan routes and keep time
2.intro: A good route saves fuel, time and stress. Plan before you drive, bike or walk.
pts: Apply route planning: group stops by area, deadlines first, use a map tool.
Compute time per stop including parking and waiting.
Check traffic, weather and construction before the first stop.
Compare two routes using distance and time, not only distance.
Calculate stops per hour from your practice route.
Add a buffer of about 15% to planned time for traffic and waiting, then adjust from your records.
Compare a loop route with going back and forth.
2.ex: Six stops: two have deadlines by noon. The route does those two first, then the rest in a loop. Planned total is 3 hours 20 minutes (200 minutes), about 33 minutes per stop. If the real run takes 3 hours 50 minutes (230 minutes), it is 30 minutes or 15% over plan, so add a buffer.
2.act: Plan and drive or walk a six-stop practice route and compare plan with real time.
2.std: Task: plan a route. Condition: six stops, two deadlines. Standard: all deadlines met and time difference explained.

3.title: Follow the rules in Canada
3.intro: Road, vehicle, tax and goods rules apply to couriers. They differ by province. Check with the local authority.
pts: Explain that a driver licence class and a vehicle registration and insurance are needed; check the use type with your insurer and provincial licensing office.
Describe hours-of-work and safe driving rules for commercial vehicles; check the current rule.
Check rules for dangerous goods, medical samples and cash; some need training or permits.
Apply tax rules: record income and costs, and check sales tax rules with the federal tax agency.
Ask the provincial licensing office which licence class your vehicle needs.
Check local rules for bike or on-foot couriers about sidewalks and bike lanes.
Keep a copy of your insurance letter and permit documents on your phone or in the vehicle.
3.ex: Rules table row: Vehicle insurance | provincial insurer | tell the insurer you use the vehicle for deliveries | before the first paid job | letter kept. If the insurer takes 5 days to reply, ask at least 5 days before the first job.
3.act: Make a rules table for your province covering licence, insurance, goods and tax, with official pages.
3.std: Task: map the rules. Condition: official pages only. Standard: each row has an enforcer, an action and a checked date.

4.title: Handle parcels and prove delivery
4.intro: Care and proof protect you and the customer.
pts: Apply handling rules: check the label, lift safely, secure items so they do not move.
Check the address, phone and name before leaving.
Build a proof routine: photo, signature or code, time, note.
Handle a failed delivery: try the contact, leave a notice, return or hold as agreed.
Leave parcels only in a place the sender has agreed to in writing.
Photograph the parcel at the door with the address visible, showing no more private information than needed.
Refuse items you cannot carry safely, such as fragile or heavy loads without help.
4.ex: Customer is not home. Courier calls, waits five minutes, leaves a notice with the time and the next try, and records it in the job log. In ten practice deliveries, 9 had full proof, which is 90%; the missing one is fixed.
4.act: Complete ten practice deliveries and record proof for each.
4.std: Task: deliver with proof. Condition: ten practice stops. Standard: every stop has a time and proof, and failed ones have a note.

5.title: Safety for you and the load
5.intro: A courier who stays safe stays in business. Rest, fitness and a safe vehicle matter.
pts: Apply safe driving: seat belt, no phone in hand, rest breaks, no rush.
Check the vehicle each day: tyres, lights, brakes, fluids, load straps.
Explain how to lift without back injury and when to ask for help.
Create an incident plan: who to call, photos, written report.
Plan rest breaks and check the rule for commercial drivers.
Prepare for winter: tyres, scraper, boots and extra time.
Report any near miss in the log with date and place.
5.ex: Daily check: tyres good, lights work, brakes fine, straps tight. Ten minutes a day is 50 minutes over a five-day week, and prevents a breakdown at noon.
5.act: Make a daily vehicle checklist and use it for one five-day week.
5.std: Task: complete safety checks. Condition: one five-day week. Standard: five dated checklists with no skipped items.

6.title: Price, costs and cash
6.intro: Courier income looks big until fuel, repair, insurance and waiting time are counted.
pts: Compute cost per kilometre: fuel, repairs, tyres, insurance, depreciation.
Compute pay per hour after costs, including time between jobs.
Compare per-stop price, per-km price and per-hour price.
Check tax set-aside for self-employment; ask an adviser.
Calculate yearly fuel cost from kilometres and fuel use.
Compare owning, leasing and renting a vehicle by total yearly cost.
Calculate the weekly profit of a client route after all costs.
6.ex: Price 12 per delivery, cost 5 in fuel and wear. Margin 7. If fixed costs are 400 a month, break-even is 400 / 7 = 57.1, so 58 deliveries. In a week, 60 deliveries x 7 = 420 over 25 hours including waiting is 16.80 an hour before fixed costs. Teaching numbers only.
6.act: Build a cost sheet for one week and find your true pay per hour.
6.std: Task: find true pay. Condition: one week of records. Standard: all costs counted and pay per hour correct.

7.title: Win clients and keep them
7.intro: Businesses want couriers who are on time and easy to reach. Reliability wins repeat work.
pts: Build a one-page offer: area, speed, price, proof, hours.
Contact local offices, clinics, shops and online sellers who need regular delivery.
Write a simple agreement: pick-up window, price, cancellation, liability.
Track the funnel: contacts, trials, regular clients.
Write the price per stop and per kilometre in the one-page offer.
Ask each trial client what would make them switch to you.
Keep a record of on-time rate to show new clients.
7.ex: Four weeks: 30 contacts, 8 trials (27%), 3 regular clients (38% of trials). The weakest step is contact to trial; offer a free first delivery.
7.act: Contact 20 businesses and book 5 trial deliveries.
7.std: Task: win regular clients. Condition: four weeks. Standard: funnel recorded and a written agreement with each regular client.

8.title: Run the courier service for real
8.intro: Now run the service with real clients, safe habits and a plan to grow.
pts: Run a 60-day pilot with a stop rule agreed in advance.
Review weekly: deliveries, on-time rate, cost per km, complaints.
Create a 12-month plan with vehicle, insurance and growth steps.
Lead others: train a second courier with your checklists and proof routine.
Calculate on-time rate as on-time deliveries divided by all deliveries.
Compare income per hour in week one and week eight.
Identify one route to add, drop or change.
8.ex: Stop rule: if on-time rate stays under 90% after 60 days, fix the plan before adding clients. Result: 192 of 200 on time is 96%; add one route.
8.act: Run the pilot, write the review and present your plan to three people.
8.std: Task: run a courier pilot. Condition: 60 days, real clients. Standard: results compared with the stop rule and insurance and licence re-checked.

quiz: What is proof of delivery?
A photo, signature or code with time that shows the parcel arrived.
Why do deadline stops go first on a route?
So the time-limited deliveries are not missed.
What must you tell your insurer?
That you use the vehicle for paid deliveries.
Who sets driver licence and vehicle rules?
The province; check your provincial office.
What do you do with dangerous goods or medical samples?
Check the rules; some need training or permits.
What do you do after a failed delivery?
Leave a notice, record it and follow the agreed return or hold step.
Name three daily vehicle checks.
Tyres, lights, brakes, fluids, straps (any three).
How do you find true pay per hour?
Income minus all costs, divided by all hours worked including waiting.
How do you find break-even deliveries?
Fixed cost divided by margin per delivery.
What belongs in a courier agreement?
Pick-up window, price, cancellation and liability.
